subject: Post-demo: data handling checkpoints & third-party access next steps
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: data handling checkpoints & third-party access next steps

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and concrete asks so we stay aligned while we circulate legal/security: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Scope: FinThrive would use Redwood for anonymized document summarization + enrichments in the underwriting flow.
- PII concern areas: SSNs, bank acct numbers, full names with DOB cross-links, and scanned documents (images).
- Residency: Primary requirement is US-only storage for any persisted artifacts; occasional processing in us-west for inference acceptable.
- Telemetry/subprocessors: we discussed the telemetry pipeline (metrics + error traces) and potential third-party analytics vendors used by FinThrive.
- Marketplace flow: you asked whether marketplace-based procurement (AWS Marketplace) would change subprocessor exposure.

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm the PII categories you consider "sensitive" for this integration (e.g., SSN + account numbers vs. name/email only)?
2) Desired max retention for any logs, transcripts, or intermediate artifacts (days).
3) List of any vendor recipients you require us to exclude (specific telemetry/analytics vendors).
4) Any contract language must-haves for processing location or subprocessors.

Attachments: I attached a draft subprocessors matrix and an initial SOW draft for discussion (see filenames below). We'll also pull a SOC 2 snapshot and SOC-related artifacts for your security team.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- Fri 5/21: FinThrive provides PII categories + retention target + vendor exclusion list.
- Mon 5/24: Redwood shares SOC 2 snapshot, brief dataflow diagram, and proposed contract paragraph options for residency & subprocessors.
- Wed 5/26: 30-min check-in with your security and procurement to close open items.

If those dates work, I'll schedule the check-in and loop in our privacy lead (Marissa) and compliance (Neha).

Best,
Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Alice Huang <alice.huang@finthrive.com>

Cc: security@finthrive.com, Bob Liao <bob.liao@ft-procure.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 17:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: data handling checkpoints & third-party access next steps

Connor — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from my side: 

1) PII categories: we treat SSNs and bank account numbers as high-risk and those must never be logged or persisted. Full name + email + transaction IDs are medium risk; hashed or tokenized storage is OK for those.
2) Retention: logs that include identifiers should be max 30 days. We can allow aggregated metrics longer.
3) Telemetry: we cannot accept data egress to known profiling vendors (we'll share a short list). We run our telemetry through an internal data lake and allow selective exports only to pre-approved analytics vendors.
4) Marketplace: procurement prefers AWS Marketplace for billing, but security wants written confirmation that marketplace procurement does not add new subprocessors without explicit approval.

I'm attaching our current data-flow diagram (sanitized) so you can see where the Redwood service would slot in. We'll pull together the vendor exclusion list and get it to you by EOD Fri.

Thanks — Alice
Product Security Manager, FinThrive
FT office: 212-555-1221

Attachment: FT-data-flow-v1.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Huang <alice.huang@finthrive.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, security@finthrive.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: data handling checkpoints & third-party access next steps

Hi Alice — looping in Redwood privacy & compliance. Appreciate the fast turnaround on the diagram. Answers and proposed controls below (quoting Connor's summary for context):

On SSNs and bank account numbers
- Redwood default behavior: we do not persist raw request inputs beyond short-lived inference caches unless explicitly configured. For high-risk PII we recommend one of two approaches:
  a) Field-level redaction on the client side prior to sending to the API; or
  b) Dedicated private deployment (VPC/private) where we can implement strict no-persist handling and customer-managed keys.

Retention and logs
- We can commit to 30-day retention for logs that include identifiers; aggregated telemetry can be kept for 13 months.
- We also support a 7-day retention policy for logs for customers who require more restrictive defaults (this is configurable per-customer for Dedicated/Private deployments).

Telemetry & subprocessors
- Outbound telemetry: minimal metrics (latency, error rates), anonymized traces only (no request bodies). By default telemetry is sent to our internal observability pipeline; telemetry vendors used by Redwood are listed in the attached subprocessors matrix.
- Marketplace procurement: marketplace billing does not inherently add subprocessors, but depending on how the marketplace handles metering/usage reporting, there may be a small set of telemetry/usage processors involved. We can add explicit contract language requiring prior approval for any new subprocessors introduced via marketplace flows.

Artifacts we can and will share
- SOC 2 snapshot and summary of scope (attached: SOC2_snapshot.pdf).
- High-level penetration test executive summary (available on request under NDA).

Proposed concrete next actions:
1) FinThrive sends vendor-exclusion list + confirmation of whether field-level redaction is feasible (due: Fri 5/21 EOD).
2) Redwood delivers redlined contract language options for residency & subprocessors and SOC2 snapshot (target: Mon 5/24).
3) 5/26 10:00 AM PT — 30-min alignment call (we'll invite procurement + security).

Connor: I'll draft the contract paragraphs and attach them to the SOW for your review. Alice/Bob: if you want an on-prem/no-persist attestation, we'll scope costs in the SOW draft.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Privacy Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
